answer: A grove council votes on buying thread to brace young trees, using funds held in a vault. Each fixed committee gets one vote per round. Its members jointly issue a credential by threshold-signing the round and ballot key; the key holder signs the ballot. Validators check both signatures and reject invalid or repeated committee credentials, including reissues. An attacker needs enough cooperating members of another committee for an extra vote. Collusion or stolen member keys can defeat this limit.
